h1: The 5 Best Laptop Locks for Microsoft Surface Laptops and Pros in 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Surface Laptop Locks: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 laptop locks for Microsoft Surface, slotless stations, adhesive plates and port anchors, compared on fit and cable.
summary: The AboveTEK locking station is the best Surface lock if the laptop lives on a desk, with adjustable arms, a 2 metre keyed cable and a pivot hinge that suits kickstand angles. The Kensington adhesive kit is the neatest portable option with a cable included, and the I3C anchor-plate lock is the proven all-rounder for under $25.
intro: Most Surface models do not have a standard lock slot, which is exactly why generic cable locks fail. The buyer mistake is picking a lock by cable thickness or length and finding out at the desk that it has nothing to plug into. The real question for a Surface is how the lock attaches: a clamp station, an adhesive plate, an anchor plate or the headphone port.

We looked at five locks that solve that problem, and compared them on attachment method, how safe the laptop finish is, which models they support and what is included in the box. This is a review of listings and spec sheets, not owner use, and we mention where a lock leaves the Surface exposed in some way.

products.name: AboveTEK MacBook and Surface Laptop Locking Station with Combo Lock Cable
products.verdict: A clamp station with a pivot hinge for kickstand-style angles and a 2 metre cable.
products.description:
The AboveTEK station uses adjustable arms for laptops 11.1 to 15.7 inches wide, dual lock clips that handle thickness, and a 78.7 inch (2 metre) keyed lock cable. A hinge pivots from 45 to 125 degrees, which is built to suit kickstand-style viewing.

It ranks first because it is the only option here designed around how a Surface is used. The pivot lets the laptop sit at the angle you like on the desk, and clamping avoids stuck-on adhesive and port blocking. The $25 to $50 price is also reasonable. The compromise is that it is a desk fixture, not a bag-friendly lock.

Buy it if a Surface Laptop or Pro lives on one desk. Skip it if you want to take the lock with you.
products.idealFor: Surface owners with a fixed desk setup.
products.skipIf: You carry the lock in a bag.

products.name: Kensington Computer Lock Adapter Kit, K60206WW
products.verdict: A small adhesive mounting plate with the NanoSaver cable lock already included.
products.description:
The K60206WW uses a 3M double-sided adhesive on a compact 1.77 by 1.77 inch mounting plate, and includes a NanoSaver cable lock so you do not need to buy one separately. The listing says the adhesive was assessed for attachment reliability.

It ranks second because it is the cleanest portable solution from a brand known for laptop security. Stick it on once and it stays, which suits a Surface kept in one place or carried between desks. The trade is permanence: adhesive is difficult to remove without risking the finish, so you are committing to the position.

Buy it if you want a portable, Kensington-branded kit with a lock included. Skip it if you want to keep the laptop's finish pristine for resale.
cons: May mark the laptop on removal
products.idealFor: Surface owners wanting a small portable lock.
products.skipIf: You plan to resell the laptop in pristine shape.

products.name: I3C Laptop Cable Lock, Hardware Security Cable Lock (1 Pack)
products.verdict: An anchor plate for Surface plus a standard-slot head, on a 6.5 foot cut-resistant cable.
products.description:
The I3C lock includes an anchor plate for Surface devices plus a standard slot laptop head, so it also works on other laptops that have a lock slot. The cable is 6.5 feet long and cut-resistant, and the price is under $25.

It ranks third because the dual head makes it useful if you own a Surface and another laptop with a standard slot, and the cable is long enough to loop around a desk leg. It is less specialised than the AboveTEK, and the anchor plate is another adhesive solution with the same removal concern.

Buy it if you want one lock that covers a Surface and a standard-slot laptop. Skip it if you want a station that avoids adhesive.

products.name: Multplx Universal Laptop Security Lock, Audio Port Anchor
products.verdict: An audio-port anchor with a 1.7 metre cable and a resettable 4-digit combination lock.
products.description:
The Multplx anchors through the audio port, names Surface as compatible, and bundles a 1.7 metre cable with a resettable 4-digit combination lock. There is no adhesive involved, so no residue risk. It costs $25 to $50.

It ranks fourth because relying on the headphone jack as an anchor point is a weaker design than a clamp or a bonded plate. It is a good deterrent, not a vault. In its favour, it leaves no marks, and everything is in one box.

Buy it if you do not want adhesive on the laptop. Skip it if you need the headphone jack while locked.
products.skipIf: You use headphones at the desk.

products.name: LORADAR Security Hardware Cable Lock Kit, Retractable Keyed
products.verdict: A self-rolling 6.2 foot cable that compresses to 4 inches, with an anchor plate for slotless Surfaces.
products.description:
The LORADAR kit fits a 3 by 7 mm keyhole directly or uses an anchor plate for slotless Surface devices. The 6.2 foot cable is self-rolling and compresses to about 4 inches, and the lock body and key are numbered for traceability. It costs under $25.

It ranks fifth because the retractable cable is a nice carrying feature, but the listing frames it for Surface Book owners, and the anchor-plate approach shares the adhesive concern. It lacks the combination of cable strength and fit detail the higher picks offer.

Buy it if you want a lock that packs small in a laptop bag. Skip it if you want a station for a fixed desk.
products.idealFor: Travelling workers who want a compact keyed lock.
products.skipIf: You want a fixed desk station.

whatMatters.detail: Most Surface models lack a standard lock slot, so a lock must clamp, bond or anchor. Clamp stations leave the laptop unmarked, adhesive plates are portable but semi-permanent, and audio-port anchors are tool-free. Decide which trade-off suits you.
A Surface Laptop, Pro and Book differ in shape and thickness. Check the width range of any station and the named models on the listing. Kickstand designs also need a lock that allows angle changes.
A cut-resistant cable resists simple snips, and length determines what you can loop around. 6 to 7 feet suits most desks. Longer cables tangle, and shorter ones limit anchor points.
Keys are quick but can be lost. Combinations cannot be lost but must be remembered, and resettable ones can be changed. Choose by who shares the lock.
Adhesive plates can leave residue or lift paint when removed. If you resell or return laptops, prefer a clamp or port anchor. Warm slowly and use gentle solvent to remove.

faq.q: Does a Surface have a lock slot?
faq.a: Most do not. Surface Laptop and Pro models lack a standard slot, so you need a station, an adhesive or anchor plate, or a port anchor.

faq.q: What is the common mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Buying a standard cable lock with no adapter. Without a slot, the lock has nothing to attach to. Choose a product designed for slotless laptops.

faq.q: Is the AboveTEK station worth it over an adhesive kit?
faq.a: If your Surface stays on a desk, yes. It adds no adhesive and supports kickstand angles. For travel, the Kensington adhesive kit is easier to carry.
Stations slide around the laptop, adhesive plates need a clean dry surface and time to bond, and port anchors push into the jack. Follow the instructions for your model.

faq.q: Do USB-C port blockers protect against theft?
faq.a: No. Port blockers stop unauthorised USB access but do not secure the laptop to a desk. Use them alongside a physical lock, not instead of one.

faq.q: Will adhesive plates damage my Surface?
faq.a: They can leave residue or lift paint if removed carelessly. Warm the plate slowly and use a gentle solvent, and consider a clamp station if you resell often.

finalTake: For a Surface on a desk, the AboveTEK locking station is the best laptop lock here because it uses no adhesive and handles kickstand angles. The Kensington adhesive kit is the better choice for carrying a lock around, and the I3C is the broadly compatible budget option. Pick the attachment method first, then the cable.
